senses.definition: (intransitive) To step or walk (on or across something); to trample.
examples: He trod back and forth wearily.

quotes.text: And Moses sware on that day, saying, Surely the land whereon thy feet haue troden, shall be thine inheritance, and thy childrens for euer, because thou hast wholly followed the Lord my God.
quotes.reference: 1611, The Holy Bible, […] (King James Version), London: […] Robert Barker, […], →OCLC, Joshua 14:9:

quotes.text: Fools rush in where angels fear to tread.

senses.definition: (transitive) To step or walk upon.
(figuratively, with certain adverbs of manner) To proceed, to behave (in a certain manner).
examples: to tread lightly, to tread gently
to tread carefully, to tread cautiously, to tread warily

senses.definition: To beat or press with the feet.
examples: to tread a path; to tread land when too light; a well-trodden path

senses.definition: To work a lever, treadle, etc., with the foot or the feet.

quotes.text: Round about them was a circle of girls and wives of the neighbouring tenants; "they trod the spinning-wheels with diligent feet, or were using the scraping carding-combs," as an author has it.

quotes.text: Through thee will we push down our enemies: through thy name will we tread them under that rise up against us.

senses.definition: The grooves carved into the face of a tire, used to give the tire traction.
The grooves on the bottom of a shoe or other footwear, used to give grip or traction.
(biology) The chalaza of a bird's egg; the treadle.
The act of avian copulation in which the male bird mounts the female by standing on her back.
(fortification) The top of the banquette, on which soldiers stand to fire over the parapet.
A bruise or abrasion produced on the foot or ankle of a horse that interferes, or strikes its feet together.
